Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

individual noun and adjective

also individuals, individually, each one, a private individual, one at a time

classical

Tac. Agr. 12.2: singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur
Phaedr. 3 prol. 49: neque enim notāre singulōs mēns est mihi
Tac. Germ. 22.1: sēparātae singulīs sēdēs et sua cuique mēnsa

singulī, singulae, singula

distributive adjective, plural; opposed to ūniversī, all together · Declension on Wiktionary

individual, one each, one by one; as a noun, individuals

Each to their own is suus cuique: sua cuique mēnsa, individual tables.

Other words

  • prīvātus, prīvātī m. — a private individual, a private citizen

    noun (the adjective prīvātus used as a noun) · also used · classical · Tac. H. 1.49: major prīvātō vīsus dum prīvātus fuit · Declension on Wiktionary

    The individual as against the state or an office-holder.

  • proprius, propria, proprium — one’s own, individual, peculiar to

    adjective, with the genitive or dative · also used · classical · Quint. 11.3.18: propria cuique est (of each person’s voice) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • homō, hominis m. — a person, an individual

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. individual (a person) · Declension on Wiktionary

  • indīviduum, indīviduī n. — an individual (of a kind or species)

    noun, second declension · avoid · medieval · M-O s.v. individual: the sense marked medieval (Dante); Cic. Fin. 1.17: corpora indīvidua (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classically “indivisible”: Cicero’s word for the atoms, indīvidua. The sense “an individual” belongs to medieval logic.

Examples

  • ita singulī pugnant, ūniversī vincuntur

    so they fight as individuals and are beaten as a wholeTac. Agr. 12.2

  • neque enim notāre singulōs mēns est mihi, vērum ipsam vītam et mōrēs hominum ostendere

    for I don’t mean to single out individuals, but to show life itself and the ways of peoplePhaedr. 3 prol. 49–50

  • lautī cibum capiunt: sēparātae singulīs sēdēs et sua cuique mēnsa

    when they have washed they eat, each at a separate seat and an individual tableTac. Germ. 22.1

See also people, separate, particular, human.
